in Youth Affairs to support the planning and delivery of the inaugural UN Youth Townhall and advance meaningful youth participation in discussions concerning technology, artificial intelligence, innovation and digital cooperation.

The individual contractor will be based in New York, United States, and will work with the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section of the United Nations Youth Office. The assignment is expected to run from September through December 2026, concluding on 31 December 2026.

This is a short-term individual-contractor assignment rather than a regular UN staff appointment. The selected professional will provide programme management, research, coordination, monitoring and policy support during a period of parental leave within the Section.

The official application deadline is 25 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. New York time, corresponding to 26 August 2026 at 03:59 UTC. Interested candidates should apply immediately through the official UN Careers vacancy page.

UN Youth Affairs Contractor Position at a Glance

Item Details
Position Programme Management Contractor, Youth Affairs
Organization United Nations
Office United Nations Youth Office
Section Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section
Job opening ID 283077
Job family Programme Management
Contract type Individual Contractor
Vacancy category Affiliate Personnel – Consultants/Individual Contractors
Job level CON
Work location New York, United States
Expected duration September–December 2026
Expected end date 31 December 2026
Date posted 17 August 2026
Application deadline 25 August 2026
Minimum education Master’s degree or equivalent
Education alternative Bachelor’s degree plus two additional years of qualifying experience
Minimum experience Two years of progressively responsible relevant experience
Required language Fluency in written and spoken English
Other languages Proficiency in another UN language is desirable
Application platform UN Inspira
Application fee None

About the United Nations Youth Office

The United Nations Youth Office was established through United Nations General Assembly Resolution 76/306 as a dedicated entity for youth affairs within the UN Secretariat.

Its mandate includes:

  • Leading system-wide coordination on youth;
  • Strengthening advocacy on youth issues;
  • Improving policy coherence concerning young people across the United Nations system;
  • Promoting meaningful youth engagement in UN processes;
  • Expanding the participation of young people in decision-making;
  • Connecting youth priorities with multilateral policy processes; and
  • Supporting coordinated action on issues affecting present and future generations.

The Office’s work is intended to ensure that young people are treated as active partners in policymaking rather than only as beneficiaries of decisions made by institutions.

Within the UN Youth Office, the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section develops strategic initiatives and partnerships that strengthen youth participation across multilateral processes. The Section also promotes collaboration among governments, UN entities, youth-led organizations, civil society, the private sector and other stakeholders.

The position is particularly connected to the Office’s growing work at the intersection of:

  • Youth participation;
  • Technology policy;
  • Digital cooperation;
  • Artificial intelligence;
  • Innovation;
  • Emerging technologies;
  • Future-ready skills; and
  • Multilateral decision-making.

More information about the Office’s mandate is available through the official United Nations Youth Office website.

Purpose of the Assignment

The selected individual contractor will provide temporary programme management and substantive support to the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section during a period of parental leave.

The assignment will continue through 31 December 2026 and concentrate on two primary workstreams:

  1. Planning and coordinating the inaugural UN Youth Townhall; and
  2. Strengthening meaningful youth engagement in technology, innovation, artificial intelligence and digital-cooperation policy processes.

The contractor will work under the supervision of the Chief of the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section and collaborate closely with colleagues throughout the UN Youth Office and the wider United Nations system.

Expected Result of Service

Successful completion of the assignment is expected to contribute to:

  • Effective planning and implementation of the inaugural UN Youth Townhall;
  • Improved coordination among UN entities and external partners;
  • Timely delivery of programme milestones;
  • Stronger monitoring and measurement of Townhall participation and impact;
  • Better documentation of stakeholder commitments and follow-up actions;
  • More coordinated youth engagement across the United Nations system;
  • Expanded opportunities for young people to participate in technology and innovation policy processes;
  • Stronger engagement between youth-led organizations and UN entities;
  • Substantive contributions to policy discussions on artificial intelligence and digital cooperation; and
  • Improved integration of youth priorities into multilateral decision-making.

The position therefore combines operational programme management with research, policy analysis, stakeholder engagement and event coordination.

About the Inaugural UN Youth Townhall

A major component of the assignment is the first UN Youth Townhall, scheduled to take place from 8 to 10 December 2026 in Heidelberg, Germany.

The Townhall is expected to bring together:

  • Young people;
  • Youth-led organizations;
  • United Nations Member States;
  • UN entities;
  • Policy experts;
  • Speakers;
  • Civil-society representatives;
  • Strategic partners; and
  • Other stakeholders working on youth participation.

The event is intended to strengthen meaningful youth engagement throughout the UN system and advance more coordinated approaches to youth participation.

Although the contractor’s official work location is New York, the vacancy states that programme support may be required before, during and after the Townhall, including on-site support where necessary. The announcement does not specify travel arrangements or whether expenses connected with Heidelberg will be separately covered.

Information about the event is available through the official UN Youth Townhall page.

Main Area One: UN Youth Townhall Programme Management

The contractor will support the day-to-day planning and implementation of the inaugural UN Youth Townhall.

Project planning

The selected candidate will develop and maintain tools needed to keep the initiative on schedule. These may include:

  • Project plans;
  • Detailed implementation schedules;
  • Milestone trackers;
  • Responsibility matrices;
  • Coordination calendars;
  • Risk registers;
  • Meeting schedules;
  • Action logs;
  • Progress dashboards; and
  • Other programme-management tools.

The contractor must monitor deadlines and ensure that responsible teams and partners remain aware of required actions.

Coordination across workstreams

The Townhall will involve several internal and external workstreams. The contractor will coordinate implementation among:

  • UN Youth Office colleagues;
  • Other United Nations entities;
  • Individual contractors;
  • External partners;
  • Member State representatives;
  • Youth organizations;
  • Speakers; and
  • Strategic collaborators.

This requires an ability to manage overlapping responsibilities, follow up on decisions and maintain clear documentation.

Monitoring, evaluation and impact measurement

The contractor will develop practical monitoring, evaluation and impact frameworks for the Townhall.

These frameworks should help assess:

  • Participation;
  • Representation;
  • Stakeholder engagement;
  • Programme outputs;
  • Commitments made during the event;
  • Quality of youth participation;
  • Immediate outcomes;
  • Follow-up actions; and
  • Longer-term learning from the Townhall.

Applicants with monitoring and evaluation experience should explain how they have designed indicators, results frameworks, tracking tools or event-assessment mechanisms.

Preparation of programme documents

The contractor will coordinate the preparation of important event and programme materials, including:

  • Concept notes;
  • Meeting agendas;
  • Briefing notes;
  • Talking points;
  • Background documents;
  • Meeting summaries;
  • Speaker information;
  • Coordination updates;
  • Progress reports; and
  • Other programme documentation.

Strong drafting, editing and information-management skills will therefore be essential.

Stakeholder engagement

The contractor will support engagement with Member States, UN entities, youth organizations, speakers and strategic partners participating in the Townhall.

This may involve:

  • Organizing coordination meetings;
  • Preparing stakeholder correspondence;
  • Recording decisions;
  • Following up on agreed actions;
  • Supporting participant engagement;
  • Consolidating inputs;
  • Maintaining contact lists; and
  • Ensuring that relevant stakeholders receive timely information.

Follow-up and institutional learning

The contractor will monitor the implementation of agreed follow-up actions and maintain programme-management records throughout the planning and delivery process.

This responsibility is important because the Townhall is intended to support continuing youth engagement rather than function only as a one-time event.

Main Area Two: Technology, Innovation and Meaningful Youth Engagement

The second major workstream concerns the participation of young people in policy discussions on technology, innovation, artificial intelligence and digital cooperation.

Monitoring UN policy processes

The contractor will follow relevant UN intergovernmental and policy processes related to:

  • Technology;
  • Digital governance;
  • Artificial intelligence;
  • Innovation;
  • Emerging technologies;
  • Digital transformation;
  • Future-ready skills; and
  • Global digital cooperation.

The contractor must identify practical opportunities for young people to participate meaningfully in these processes.

Supporting youth participation

The role involves moving beyond symbolic consultation and creating opportunities for young people to contribute to policy discussions and decision-making.

This may include:

  • Engaging youth-led organizations;
  • Consulting young technology experts;
  • Connecting young people with UN policy processes;
  • Supporting youth participation in meetings or consultations;
  • Consolidating youth perspectives;
  • Preparing substantive inputs based on youth priorities; and
  • Linking outreach initiatives with concrete participation opportunities.

Partner and institutional coordination

Under the leadership of the Chief of the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Section, the contractor will serve as a focal point for engagement with relevant partners and entities.

The vacancy specifically identifies:

  • The International Telecommunication Union;
  • The Office of Digital and Emerging Technologies;
  • Global Digital Compact implementation processes;
  • The UN Innovation Network;
  • The UN 2.0 initiative; and
  • Other stakeholders working on technology, innovation and digital cooperation.

The contractor must be capable of maintaining professional relationships across multiple institutions and translating discussions into clear actions, materials and follow-up.

Policy research and analysis

The contractor will prepare substantive inputs, policy analysis and briefing materials related to:

  • Artificial intelligence;
  • Technology policy;
  • Emerging technologies;
  • Digital cooperation;
  • Innovation;
  • Youth policy; and
  • Future-ready skills.

Applicants should be able to analyse complex information and explain it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Coordination with communications colleagues

The contractor will work with communications personnel to connect public outreach and advocacy on artificial intelligence and future-ready skills with actual opportunities for youth participation.

This could involve aligning:

  • Communications campaigns;
  • Policy events;
  • Youth consultations;
  • Partner engagement;
  • Digital content;
  • Advocacy messages; and
  • Participation pathways.

Main Area Three: Programme and Substantive Support

In addition to the two principal workstreams, the contractor will support the Section’s broader priorities.

Responsibilities include:

  • Conducting research on assigned issues;
  • Preparing analytical inputs;
  • Drafting briefing notes;
  • Producing written materials;
  • Supporting coordination among UN entities;
  • Liaising with external partners;
  • Contributing to internal planning;
  • Supporting reporting processes;
  • Maintaining programme documentation;
  • Assisting with priority initiatives; and
  • Performing other related duties assigned by the supervisor.

Education Requirements

Applicants must hold an advanced university degree, normally a Master’s degree or equivalent, in one of the following areas:

  • International relations;
  • Public policy;
  • Political science;
  • Public administration;
  • Development studies;
  • Innovation;
  • Technology policy; or
  • Another closely related field.

The degree should provide a credible academic foundation for programme management, policy analysis, international cooperation, youth affairs or technology-governance work.

Alternative education pathway

A first-level university degree, normally a Bachelor’s degree, may be accepted instead of a Master’s degree when combined with two additional years of qualifying professional experience.

Since the vacancy separately requires at least two years of relevant experience, applicants relying on the Bachelor’s-degree alternative should generally be prepared to demonstrate approximately four years of qualifying experience.

The final determination of education equivalency and qualifying experience rests with the United Nations.

Required Professional Experience

Applicants must have at least two years of progressively responsible experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Programme management;
  • Policy;
  • International development; or
  • A related professional field.

“Progressively responsible” generally means that the applicant’s duties, independence, complexity or accountability increased over time.

Candidates should provide specific examples of:

  • Managing projects or programmes;
  • Coordinating implementation timelines;
  • Working with multiple partners;
  • Preparing analytical documents;
  • Tracking project results;
  • Supporting policy processes;
  • Organizing international initiatives; or
  • Managing institutional relationships.

Desirable Professional Experience

The following experience is desirable rather than mandatory:

Multilateral and intergovernmental processes

Experience supporting multilateral processes, stakeholder engagement or intergovernmental coordination is desirable.

Relevant examples could include work with:

  • United Nations entities;
  • International organizations;
  • Government ministries;
  • Diplomatic missions;
  • Regional organizations;
  • International conferences;
  • Intergovernmental negotiations; or
  • Multistakeholder policy platforms.

Complex initiatives and international events

Experience coordinating complex multistakeholder initiatives or international events is desirable.

Candidates should highlight experience involving:

  • Multiple workstreams;
  • International participants;
  • Senior-level speakers;
  • Government representatives;
  • Event logistics;
  • Programme design;
  • Partner coordination;
  • Briefing materials;
  • Results tracking; or
  • Post-event follow-up.

Youth, technology and digital policy

Experience in one or more of the following areas is desirable:

  • Youth policy;
  • Youth participation;
  • Technology policy;
  • Innovation;
  • Artificial intelligence;
  • Digital governance;
  • Digital cooperation;
  • Future-ready skills; or
  • Emerging technologies.

Monitoring and evaluation

Experience developing monitoring, evaluation or results-tracking frameworks is also desirable.

This could include:

  • Results frameworks;
  • Logical frameworks;
  • Indicators;
  • Monitoring plans;
  • Evaluation tools;
  • Data-collection instruments;
  • Outcome tracking;
  • Event-impact assessment; or
  • Reporting dashboards.

Language Requirements

Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

For UN applications, fluency generally requires a high level of proficiency in:

  • Reading;
  • Writing;
  • Speaking; and
  • Understanding.

Applicants should accurately record their English proficiency in the Inspira application.

Proficiency in another United Nations language is desirable. The other official UN languages are:

  • Arabic;
  • Chinese;
  • French;
  • Russian; and
  • Spanish.

Additional language ability should be included only where the applicant can accurately describe the level of proficiency.

Skills Likely to Be Important

Although the vacancy does not present a separate competency list, its responsibilities indicate that the following capabilities will be important:

  • Programme and project management;
  • Stakeholder coordination;
  • Strategic planning;
  • Policy research;
  • Analytical writing;
  • Briefing preparation;
  • Monitoring and evaluation;
  • Results tracking;
  • Event coordination;
  • Partnership management;
  • Professional communication;
  • Time management;
  • Attention to detail;
  • Ability to work across institutions;
  • Understanding of meaningful youth engagement;
  • Knowledge of technology and digital-policy issues;
  • Ability to manage competing deadlines; and
  • Professional judgment in a multilateral environment.

Contract Conditions and Compensation

This vacancy is classified as an Individual Contractor opportunity under the UN category of Affiliate Personnel – Consultants/Individual Contractors.

It is not advertised as a regular United Nations staff position and does not carry a Professional staff grade such as P-2, P-3 or P-4.

The vacancy does not publish:

  • The contract fee;
  • Monthly or daily remuneration;
  • Payment schedule;
  • Health-insurance arrangements;
  • Pension entitlement;
  • Leave provisions;
  • Relocation support;
  • Visa sponsorship;
  • Travel reimbursement;
  • Accommodation support; or
  • Remote-working arrangements.

Applicants should not assume that regular UN staff benefits apply to this contract. Any compensation, travel and administrative arrangements should be confirmed during the recruitment or contracting process.

Work Location and Possible Travel

The official work location is:

New York, United States

The assignment is therefore not advertised as home-based or remote.

Because the contractor will support the UN Youth Townhall in Heidelberg, Germany, including on-site support where required, travel may form part of the assignment. However, the vacancy does not state:

  • Whether travel is mandatory;
  • Who will cover travel expenses;
  • Whether daily subsistence allowance will be provided;
  • Whether the contractor must already hold permission to travel; or
  • How many days of on-site support will be required.

Applicants should seek clarification if they progress in the recruitment process.

How to Apply Through UN Inspira

Applications must be submitted through Inspira, the United Nations’ online talent-management platform.

Step 1: Open the vacancy

Visit the official vacancy announcement and select “Apply Now.”

Step 2: Log in or create an Inspira account

External candidates require an Inspira account before submitting an application. New applicants must provide basic information such as their name, email address and date of birth.

Step 3: Complete the candidate profile

Applicants must complete the mandatory profile fields before an application can be submitted. Information may include:

  • Personal details;
  • Nationality and residence;
  • Education;
  • Employment history;
  • Language proficiency;
  • Training and certifications;
  • Publications;
  • Professional references; and
  • Other relevant qualifications.

Step 4: Answer the job-requirement questions

The application may include screening questions based on the vacancy’s education, experience and language requirements.

Each answer should be supported by details elsewhere in the application. Simply selecting “yes” without providing corresponding evidence in the work-history or education sections may not be sufficient.

Step 5: Detail relevant work experience

For each position, applicants should explain:

  • The employer or organization;
  • The period of employment;
  • The exact role;
  • Principal responsibilities;
  • Programme or project scope;
  • Stakeholders involved;
  • Results achieved;
  • Supervisory responsibilities, where applicable; and
  • Relevance to this UN assignment.

Step 6: Complete the motivation statement

The motivation statement should explain why the applicant is interested in the assignment and how their experience meets the UN Youth Office’s needs.

It should not merely repeat the CV. Instead, it should connect the candidate’s strongest experience with:

  • Youth engagement;
  • Programme management;
  • International events;
  • Stakeholder coordination;
  • Technology policy;
  • Digital cooperation;
  • Monitoring and evaluation; and
  • Multilateral work.

Step 7: Review and submit

Applicants should review every section carefully before selecting “Certify and Submit.”

The official UN applicant guidance states that submitted applications cannot be edited. An applicant may withdraw a submission but cannot submit another application to the same vacancy.

Detailed instructions are available through the official UN Careers application guide.

How to Make the Application Competitive

Quantify programme-management experience

Do not write only that you “supported programme management.” Explain:

  • The size of the programme;
  • Number and type of stakeholders;
  • Geographic coverage;
  • Budget or resources managed, where appropriate;
  • Major deadlines;
  • Tools developed;
  • Challenges resolved; and
  • Results achieved.

Demonstrate monitoring and evaluation ability

Provide examples of indicators, monitoring plans, evaluation tools, dashboards or results frameworks that you developed or used.

Show multistakeholder coordination

Describe experience coordinating governments, international organizations, youth groups, civil society, private-sector partners or technical experts.

Highlight strong writing skills

Identify concept notes, policy briefs, talking points, reports, agendas, meeting summaries or analytical papers that you have prepared.

Connect youth participation with policy influence

Strong applicants should distinguish meaningful youth participation from basic outreach. Explain how young people were enabled to contribute to programme design, policy dialogue or decision-making.

Address technology and digital cooperation

Candidates with experience in artificial intelligence, digital policy, innovation or emerging technologies should explain the policy relevance of their work, not only its technical aspects.

Tailor the motivation statement

The motivation statement should directly address the contractor’s two principal workstreams:

  1. Delivering the UN Youth Townhall; and
  2. Expanding meaningful youth engagement in technology and digital-policy processes.

Application Deadline

The UN Careers listing gives the closing date as:

25 August 2026

The underlying recruitment system closes the application at:

25 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. New York time

This is equivalent to:

  • 26 August 2026 at 03:59 UTC
  • 26 August 2026 at 08:59 a.m. Pakistan Standard Time

Applications cannot be submitted after the closing time. Candidates should apply several hours early to avoid login, document-upload or internet problems.

Recruitment Fee and Fraud Warning

The United Nations does not charge any fee at any stage of recruitment, including:

  • Application;
  • Interview;
  • Processing;
  • Training; or
  • Appointment-related communication.

The United Nations also does not request applicants’ bank-account information as part of the recruitment process.

Any person requesting payment in connection with this vacancy should be treated as potentially fraudulent.

Conclusion

The UN Youth Office Programme Management Contractor position offers a short-term opportunity to support a major international youth-engagement initiative while contributing to policy work on technology, artificial intelligence, innovation and digital cooperation.

The assignment is particularly suitable for professionals who combine programme-management experience with strong research, writing, stakeholder-coordination and monitoring skills. Experience in youth policy, international events, multilateral processes or technology governance would provide a significant advantage.

The selected contractor will work from New York from September through December 2026 and support the inaugural UN Youth Townhall scheduled for 8–10 December 2026 in Heidelberg, Germany.

Because the application deadline is 25 August 2026, qualified applicants should complete and submit their Inspira applications immediately.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies at the University of Birmingham in the United Kingdom. This is a full-time, salaried postdoctoral appointment for an early-career historian currently based in Africa and affiliated with an African higher education institution.

The successful candidate will join the University of Birmingham’s School of History and Cultures for an 18-month fellowship beginning on 1 January 2027. The Fellow will undertake an agreed programme of research in African History, produce academic publications, contribute to the University’s research community and support undergraduate and postgraduate teaching in History and African Studies.

The position carries a starting salary of £36,636 to £46,049 per year, with the potential to progress to £48,822 once in post. It is classified at Grade 7 and offered on a fixed-term contract running up to June 2028.

The official application deadline is 1 September 2026. Applicants should apply electronically through the University of Birmingham’s official recruitment portal.

Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at a Glance

Item Details
Position Research Fellow, Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship in African Studies
Host institution University of Birmingham
School School of History and Cultures
Academic area African History and African Studies
Location Edgbaston, Birmingham, United Kingdom
Contract Full-time, fixed-term
Fellowship duration Approximately 18 months
Expected start date 1 January 2027
Contract end Up to June 2028
Salary £36,636–£46,049 per year
Potential progression Up to £48,822 once in post
Grade Grade 7
Job category Academic Non-clinical
Job function Research
Job reference 107675
Oracle job identification 9655
Posting date 24 July 2026
Application deadline 1 September 2026
Application method Online through the University’s recruitment system
Informal enquiries Dr Juliet Gilbert at j.gilbert.2@bham.ac.uk

About the Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship

The Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship is connected to the University of Birmingham’s long-standing work with African scholars and higher education institutions. The post is funded through an endowment intended to enable academics affiliated with African universities to spend a sustained period at the University of Birmingham.

The University’s broader Cadbury Research Fellowship Scheme has supported collaborative academic activities between Birmingham researchers and scholars based at African institutions. The programme has historically offered early-career researchers opportunities to develop their work through engagement with the University’s academic community, research collections and scholarly networks.

The University explains that Cadbury-supported scholars may become involved in academic activities such as:

  • Presentations of research in progress;
  • Reading and writing groups;
  • Research seminars;
  • Research-methods activities;
  • Meetings with academic colleagues;
  • Collaborative research discussions; and
  • Engagement with the University’s library and research collections.

The precise responsibilities and support arrangements for this 18-month post are governed by the current vacancy announcement and employment contract. Additional background is available through the University’s Cadbury Research Fellowship Scheme page.

Purpose of the Fellowship

The University of Birmingham is seeking a Postdoctoral Fellow in African History who can contribute meaningfully to both research and teaching.

The successful candidate will pursue a programme of research agreed with an academic mentor. This structure is intended to allow the Fellow to advance an independent research and publication agenda while benefiting from intellectual guidance and participation in the wider research environment of the School of History and Cultures.

The Fellowship is not limited to personal research. The successful applicant will also be expected to contribute to:

  • The research culture of the relevant department;
  • Academic activities across the School of History and Cultures;
  • The broader University research community;
  • Teaching in History and African Studies;
  • Student research supervision;
  • Public engagement;
  • Academic administration; and
  • Equality, diversity and inclusion within the workplace.

Main Research Responsibilities

Research is a central component of the Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship. The successful candidate will be expected to undertake high-quality research within their historical area of specialization.

The principal research responsibilities include:

1. Developing research objectives and proposals

The Fellow will develop clear research objectives for individual or collaborative work. The successful candidate may receive assistance from a mentor where appropriate, but must demonstrate the ability to define a focused, realistic and academically significant research programme.

2. Conducting research in African History

The research must fall within African History or a closely connected area of African Studies. The person specification particularly requires candidates to be capable of constructing a convincing and achievable research and publication proposal in African History.

The applicant’s work may relate to Africa itself, African diasporas or historical connections between African societies and wider global developments, provided that the project has a clear historical foundation.

3. Collecting and analysing research material

The Fellow will collect and evaluate research data or evidence using methods appropriate to the project. Depending on the nature of the proposed research, this may include:

  • Archival research;
  • Literature reviews;
  • Oral-history interviews;
  • Qualitative research interviews;
  • Documentary analysis;
  • Comparative historical analysis;
  • Digital research methods; and
  • Other relevant research techniques.

The Fellow must be able to analyse and interpret findings accurately and connect them to wider historical debates.

4. Producing new intellectual understanding

The successful candidate will be expected to apply subject knowledge in ways that develop original scholarly arguments and contribute new understanding to African History or African Studies.

This means that the proposed project should not merely repeat the applicant’s doctoral thesis. It should demonstrate a credible postdoctoral trajectory, showing how previous doctoral work will be developed, extended or redirected into a distinct programme of research and publication.

5. Disseminating research findings

The Fellow will be responsible for communicating research findings through appropriate academic channels. Expected outputs may include:

  • Peer-reviewed journal articles;
  • Book chapters;
  • A monograph proposal or manuscript;
  • Conference papers;
  • Departmental research seminars;
  • Research posters;
  • Workshops;
  • Public lectures; and
  • Other academic or public-facing outputs.

The job description specifically requires the preparation and presentation of research outputs, including drafting academic publications or sections of publications.

6. Managing research challenges and deadlines

The Fellow must identify and address problems that could prevent the research project from meeting its objectives or deadlines. This requires strong research planning, time management and the ability to adjust methods or priorities when unexpected difficulties arise.

Teaching Responsibilities

The Fellowship includes a substantial teaching contribution in History and African Studies.

The successful candidate must be able to support teaching at undergraduate and Master’s level. Responsibilities may include some or all of the following:

  • Convening undergraduate modules;
  • Convening postgraduate modules;
  • Delivering lectures;
  • Leading seminars and tutorials;
  • Designing teaching materials;
  • Preparing student assessments;
  • Marking assignments and examinations;
  • Providing academic feedback;
  • Supervising undergraduate dissertations;
  • Supervising postgraduate dissertations;
  • Supporting broader teaching-related activities; and
  • Contributing to programme and curriculum development.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate more than research excellence. Evidence of effective university-level teaching, student support, assessment or curriculum development will strengthen an application.

Candidates with limited formal teaching experience should clearly explain any related experience, such as:

  • Teaching assistantships;
  • Guest lectures;
  • Seminar facilitation;
  • Student mentoring;
  • Dissertation support;
  • Academic workshops;
  • Research-methods training; or
  • Curriculum-development activities.

Student Supervision and Academic Guidance

The successful Fellow may supervise students undertaking research-related work. Where appropriate to the discipline and level of experience, the Fellow may also provide guidance to doctoral researchers.

The role may involve:

  • Advising students on research methods;
  • Providing feedback on research plans;
  • Supporting students who assist with a research project;
  • Helping students interpret historical evidence;
  • Advising on academic writing;
  • Supporting dissertation development; and
  • Referring more complex supervisory matters to senior academic staff where necessary.

Contribution to the University’s Research Environment

The Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellow will be expected to participate actively in the academic life of the department, School and wider University.

This may involve:

  • Attending research seminars;
  • Presenting work in progress;
  • Participating in reading and writing groups;
  • Contributing to workshops and conferences;
  • Collaborating with researchers in related fields;
  • Supporting departmental research initiatives;
  • Assisting with research-related administration;
  • Contributing to new research methods or analytical approaches; and
  • Building connections between the University of Birmingham and African higher education institutions.

The Fellow should approach the position as an active member of an academic community rather than solely as an individual researcher using University facilities.

Management and Administrative Responsibilities

The position also includes administrative duties arising from research and teaching activities.

The successful candidate may be expected to:

  • Organize research-related activities;
  • Support seminars or workshops;
  • Maintain research records;
  • Coordinate parts of a module;
  • Participate in departmental meetings;
  • Assist with student administration;
  • Contribute to reporting requirements;
  • Manage research deadlines;
  • Support research or teaching teams; and
  • contribute to broader School or University processes.

Applicants must therefore show that they can manage responsibilities reliably, communicate effectively with colleagues and contribute to institutional processes.

Public Engagement Responsibilities

The Fellow may contribute to public engagement activities that support the strategic objectives of the School, College and University.

Public engagement could involve communicating research to audiences beyond universities, including:

  • Schools;
  • Museums;
  • Cultural organizations;
  • Community groups;
  • Policymakers;
  • Media organizations;
  • Research participants; and
  • Members of the general public.

Candidates whose work already includes community engagement, public history, digital scholarship or collaboration with cultural organizations should explain how that experience could support the role.

Essential Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet every essential condition stated in the person specification.

PhD requirement

Candidates must hold a PhD focused on:

  • The history of Africa;
  • The history of African diasporas; or
  • A closely related historical subject that clearly addresses Africa or African diasporic communities.

The PhD must have been formally examined and passed between:

1 June 2021 and 1 June 2026

This is a strict eligibility period.

Candidates who have submitted their doctoral thesis but are still waiting for examination or final approval are explicitly ineligible. The doctorate must already have been examined and passed by the prescribed date.

Current location requirement

Applicants must currently be based on the African continent.

The formal person specification does not restrict eligibility to a particular African nationality. The requirement concerns the applicant’s current location and institutional affiliation.

Institutional affiliation requirement

Applicants must be employed by or otherwise affiliated with an African higher education institution.

Depending on the circumstances, acceptable affiliation may include employment, an academic appointment or another formally recognized institutional relationship. Candidates should ensure that their application clearly identifies:

  • The institution’s official name;
  • The applicant’s current position or status;
  • The nature of the institutional relationship; and
  • Contact information or documentation that can verify the affiliation.

Permanent academic position requirement

Applicants must meet one of the following two conditions:

  1. They do not currently hold a permanent academic position; or
  2. If they hold a permanent academic position, they must submit a statement confirming that their home institution will release them for the full period of the University of Birmingham appointment.

A permanently employed academic is therefore not automatically excluded. However, the required institutional release statement must accompany the application.

Research Experience and Publication Requirements

Candidates must provide evidence of research activity and publications appropriate to their level of postdoctoral experience.

The University does not prescribe a fixed number of publications in the vacancy. Candidates will instead be evaluated relative to their career stage and the time elapsed since completing the PhD.

Relevant evidence may include:

  • Peer-reviewed journal articles;
  • Book chapters;
  • Research reports;
  • An academic monograph;
  • An accepted book proposal;
  • Edited collections;
  • Policy or public-history publications;
  • Conference presentations;
  • Research grants;
  • Research projects;
  • Archival or fieldwork experience; and
  • Research collaboration.

Applicants should distinguish clearly between published, accepted, forthcoming and under-review work.

Research and Publication Proposal

A competitive applicant must be able to construct a persuasive and achievable research and publication proposal in African History.

The proposal should normally explain:

  1. The proposed research topic;
  2. The central research questions;
  3. The significance of the project;
  4. The relationship to existing scholarship;
  5. The proposed methodology;
  6. The evidence or sources to be used;
  7. The work already completed;
  8. The activities planned during the Fellowship;
  9. The expected publication outputs;
  10. A realistic 18-month timetable;
  11. The relevance of the University of Birmingham’s expertise or resources; and
  12. The broader contribution to African History and African Studies.

The vacancy does not publish a specific proposal word limit. Applicants should follow any limits or upload instructions shown inside the online application system.

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Requirements

Applicants must understand the protected characteristics and institutional responsibilities established under the United Kingdom’s Equality Act 2010.

The successful Fellow will be expected to:

  • Foster positive working relationships;
  • Support a fair and equitable workplace;
  • Recognize equality and diversity issues;
  • Respond appropriately to discrimination or exclusion;
  • Follow relevant University policies;
  • Contribute to the University’s Public Sector Equality Duty; and
  • Help create an inclusive environment for staff and students.

The University of Birmingham states that diversity supports the exchange of ideas, innovation and academic debate. It holds Athena SWAN, Race Equality Charter and Disability Confident accreditations and operates an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Centre.

Salary and Contract Conditions

The normal starting salary is:

£36,636 to £46,049 per year

The position offers potential progression to:

£48,822 per year once in post

The final starting salary within the published range will normally depend on the University’s appointment policies and the successful candidate’s experience.

The appointment is:

  • Full-time;
  • Grade 7;
  • Fixed-term;
  • Expected to begin on 1 January 2027; and
  • Scheduled to continue up to June 2028.

This produces an approximate appointment period of 18 months.

The vacancy does not specify a separate research allowance, relocation payment, accommodation package or travel budget. Applicants should not assume that these expenses are automatically covered.

What the Fellowship Can Offer

The primary confirmed financial benefit is the published salary. Professionally, the appointment may also provide the successful candidate with opportunities to:

  • Develop an independent postdoctoral research programme;
  • Work with an academic mentor;
  • Produce peer-reviewed publications;
  • Gain teaching experience at undergraduate and Master’s levels;
  • Develop module-convening and assessment experience;
  • Supervise student research;
  • Participate in an established research environment;
  • Access University research resources and collections;
  • Build international research networks;
  • Strengthen links with African and United Kingdom institutions;
  • Develop public engagement experience; and
  • Build a stronger profile for future academic appointments or research funding.

These professional outcomes will depend on the Fellow’s project, activities and performance during the appointment.

Application Documents to Prepare

The full attachment list should be confirmed inside the recruitment portal. Based on the published requirements, applicants should be prepared to provide:

  • An updated academic curriculum vitae;
  • A tailored cover letter or supporting statement;
  • Details of the completed PhD;
  • Evidence that the PhD was examined and passed within the eligible period;
  • A research and publication proposal;
  • A complete publication list;
  • Evidence of teaching experience;
  • Evidence of research activity;
  • Details of the current African higher education affiliation;
  • A release statement from the home institution if the applicant holds a permanent academic position; and
  • Any additional information requested through the online form.

Candidates should use the exact names of qualifications, institutions, positions and publications. Unsupported or exaggerated claims could weaken the application.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted electronically through the University of Birmingham recruitment portal.

Step 1: Review the eligibility conditions

Before beginning the form, confirm that:

  • Your PhD is in African History, African diaspora history or an appropriately related historical field;
  • Your PhD was examined and passed between 1 June 2021 and 1 June 2026;
  • You are currently based in Africa;
  • You are employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution; and
  • You can provide a release statement if you hold a permanent academic appointment.

Step 2: Prepare a focused research proposal

Ensure that the project is achievable within 18 months and produces clear scholarly outputs. Avoid proposing a project so broad that it cannot be completed during the appointment.

Step 3: Tailor the supporting statement

The supporting statement should directly address each point in the person specification. Use clear evidence rather than general claims.

Step 4: Update the academic CV

Place the most relevant information prominently, including:

  • PhD title and completion date;
  • Research interests;
  • Publications;
  • Current institutional affiliation;
  • Teaching experience;
  • Research projects;
  • Conference presentations;
  • Public engagement; and
  • Administrative or leadership responsibilities.

Step 5: Secure the release statement if required

Applicants in permanent academic positions should obtain the required statement before the deadline. The statement should confirm that the home institution will release the applicant for the full period of appointment at the University of Birmingham.

Step 6: Complete the official online application

Submit the application through the official University of Birmingham vacancy page.

Step 7: Submit before the deadline

Do not wait until the final day. Upload and system problems may prevent a late application from being considered.

Important Warning About the Use of Artificial Intelligence

The University has included a specific warning about using artificial intelligence in applications.

It wants the written elements to demonstrate the candidate’s genuine interest and personal communication style. Applications that rely too heavily on AI may appear generic and may not provide enough specific evidence for the selection panel to evaluate the applicant’s experience and suitability.

The University states that applications which rely excessively on AI are unlikely to progress to the interview stage.

Applicants should therefore:

  • Write in their own voice;
  • Use evidence drawn from their real experience;
  • Tailor every answer to the role;
  • Check all dates and publication details;
  • Avoid generic statements;
  • Do not invent experience or achievements; and
  • Personally review and revise every submitted document.

How to Strengthen an Application

A strong application should demonstrate an exact match between the candidate’s experience and the person specification.

Research fit

Explain why the project belongs within African History and how it contributes to current scholarly debates.

Feasibility

Show that the research and publication plan can realistically be delivered during an 18-month appointment.

Publication pathway

Identify specific expected outputs rather than promising only to “publish research.” State whether the project is expected to produce articles, chapters, a monograph proposal or other defined outputs.

Institutional value

Explain how the applicant will contribute to the School of History and Cultures through research seminars, teaching, collaboration, student supervision and public engagement.

Teaching readiness

Provide specific examples of modules taught, seminars delivered, assessments designed, dissertations supervised or students supported.

African institutional connection

Explain how the Fellowship could support continuing research relationships between the University of Birmingham and the applicant’s home institution.

Equality and inclusion

Provide evidence of creating inclusive teaching, research or workplace environments instead of merely stating support for equality.

Deadline

The official closing date is:

1 September 2026

The live University of Birmingham portal currently displays this deadline. Some older third-party reposts may show an earlier closing date, but applicants should follow the current official vacancy page and apply as soon as possible.

Informal Enquiries

Questions about the academic scope of the Fellowship may be directed to:

Dr Juliet Gilbert
Email: j.gilbert.2@bham.ac.uk

This address is for informal enquiries. Applications must still be submitted through the official online recruitment system.

Applicants may wish to seek clarification regarding matters not stated in the vacancy, including:

  • Visa sponsorship;
  • Relocation expenses;
  • Travel support;
  • Accommodation;
  • Research funding;
  • The expected teaching load;
  • The identity or selection of the academic mentor;
  • Research-proposal length;
  • Permitted start-date flexibility; and
  • Documentation required to confirm institutional affiliation.

Conclusion

The University of Birmingham Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship in African Studies provides a substantial opportunity for an Africa-based early-career historian to develop an independent research and publication programme in the United Kingdom.

With an 18-month appointment, a starting salary of £36,636 to £46,049, possible progression to £48,822 and opportunities to contribute to both research and teaching, the position can support the Fellow’s development as a scholar, teacher and member of an international academic community.

Eligibility is tightly defined. Applicants must already hold an eligible PhD, must be based on the African continent and must be employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution. Candidates in permanent academic positions must also provide confirmation that their institution will release them for the duration of the Birmingham appointment.

Qualified applicants should prepare a carefully tailored research proposal, academic CV and supporting statement and submit through the official recruitment portal before 1 September 2026.

For more global opportunities, click HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The Tech Policy Press Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from professionals interested in exploring important questions at the intersection of technology, democracy and society. The year-long, part-time fellowship provides selected fellows with a $10,000 stipend, editorial guidance, an international professional network and opportunities to produce public-interest reporting and analysis.

Applications for the 2027 cohort must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. EDT on September 24, 2026.

The fellowship is designed to support individuals who have established expertise in a particular technology policy issue, geography or broader area involving technology’s impact on democracy and society. Tech Policy Press is particularly interested in work that brings attention to communities and regions that have historically been excluded from global technology policy discussions.

About the Tech Policy Press Fellowship

Tech Policy Press launched its fellowship program in 2023. Since its launch, the program has supported 25 fellows from 11 countries across three cohorts.

Previous fellows have explored important issues including:

  • Artificial intelligence governance
  • Technology regulation
  • Digital rights
  • The relationship between state power and corporate power
  • Technology’s impact on democracy and society
  • Other pressing technology policy questions

For the 2027 cohort, Tech Policy Press is looking for a new group of fellows who can contribute meaningful reporting and analysis on urgent and underreported issues at the intersection of technology and democracy.

The fellowship is structured as a 12-month, part-time program beginning in January 2027. Fellows will work remotely as independent contractors.

What the 2027 Fellowship Offers

One of the major benefits of the program is the financial support provided to each selected fellow.

$10,000 Fellowship Stipend

Each fellow will receive a $10,000 stipend to support their work during the fellowship.

The stipend will be distributed quarterly, allowing fellows to receive financial support throughout the year as they work on their projects.

Editorial Guidance

Fellows will receive ongoing editorial guidance from the Tech Policy Press team. This support is intended to help fellows strengthen their reporting, analysis and overall body of work.

International Fellowship Cohort

Selected fellows will become part of an international cohort of current fellows who can exchange ideas, provide feedback and collaborate where appropriate.

This creates an opportunity to build relationships with professionals working on technology policy and related issues in different countries and regions.

Monthly Learning and Exchange Sessions

Fellows will participate in monthly sessions designed to support and strengthen their work. These sessions provide opportunities for learning, discussion, feedback and the exchange of ideas.

Opportunity to Build a Significant Body of Work

Over the course of the 12-month fellowship, participants will have the opportunity to develop a substantial body of reporting and analysis around an important technology policy issue.

The fellowship can therefore provide a structured environment for professionals who want to deepen their expertise and produce high-quality public-interest work.

Visibility Through Tech Policy Press

Tech Policy Press plans to publish fellows’ work on its website and feature it prominently in its newsletter.

Fellowship projects may also be highlighted through:

  • The Tech Policy Press podcast
  • Special events
  • Other opportunities to showcase fellows’ work

This can provide fellows with an opportunity to reach both the general public and decision-makers interested in technology policy.

Areas of Work for Fellows

Applicants are expected to have a clear area of focus and explain how their proposed work can contribute to public understanding and decision-making.

The fellowship welcomes work related to a wide range of technology policy topics.

Potential areas may include:

  • Artificial intelligence governance
  • Technology regulation
  • Digital rights
  • Technology and democracy
  • Technology and society
  • Digital governance
  • State and corporate power
  • Technology policy in particular countries or regions
  • Underreported technology policy issues
  • The impact of technology on communities
  • Other issues that fall within Tech Policy Press’s editorial focus

Applicants do not necessarily have to restrict themselves to one specific topic throughout the entire fellowship. The program encourages fellows to respond to relevant news and developments as they relate to their area of expertise.

Focus on Underrepresented Communities and Regions

Tech Policy Press is particularly interested in projects that center communities and regions that are often left out of global technology policy conversations.

This makes the fellowship especially relevant for applicants who can bring perspectives, expertise or reporting from areas that are not adequately represented in mainstream technology policy discussions.

There is no specific preferred geographic or thematic focus for applicants from the Global South, according to the fellowship’s frequently asked questions.

Fellowship Responsibilities and Expectations

Successful fellows will have a number of responsibilities throughout the 12-month program.

1. Produce Regular Reporting or Analysis

Fellows will be expected to contribute reporting or analysis related to technology and democracy at least once per month.

Although topics may evolve after the fellowship begins, applicants should clearly explain:

  • The topic they intend to focus on
  • Why the issue is important
  • Why they are well positioned to cover it
  • How their work will contribute to public understanding and decision-making

2. Attend Monthly Cohort Meetings

Fellows must attend a mandatory one-hour monthly cohort meeting.

These meetings provide an opportunity for fellows to connect with one another and participate in the fellowship’s collaborative learning environment.

3. Attend Monthly Editorial Check-Ins

Fellows will also participate in monthly meetings with the Tech Policy Press editorial team.

These meetings will be used to:

  • Review progress
  • Discuss challenges
  • Evaluate upcoming work
  • Determine next steps

4. Collaborate With Other Fellows

Fellows may be expected to collaborate with other members of the fellowship cohort and the Tech Policy Press masthead when appropriate.

5. Meet Agreed Deadlines

Participants must meet all deadlines agreed upon with the Tech Policy Press team for their work and other fellowship outputs.

6. Disclose Conflicts of Interest

Fellows are expected to disclose any potential conflicts of interest connected to their work.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship welcomes applications from professionals including:

  • Journalists
  • Researchers
  • Lawyers
  • Public policy professionals

APPLY HERE

Applicants should have a demonstrated interest or background in technology policy, media or a related field and be committed to producing high-quality public-interest work during the fellowship.

Applicants should also be able to demonstrate strong expertise in a particular technology policy issue, geography or broader area involving technology’s impact on democracy or society.

Tech Policy Press encourages applications from the Global Majority and communities that are underrepresented in media.

International Applicants Are Welcome

The 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship is open to applicants internationally.

The organization specifically confirms that international applicants are encouraged to apply and that the fellowship is open to candidates from around the world.

Applicants outside the United States do not need to be authorized to work in the United States to participate in the fellowship.

All fellows will work remotely as independent contractors.

What Counts as Published Work?

Applicants are required to provide links to previous publications.

A qualifying published work should:

  • Be publicly accessible online
  • Clearly identify the applicant as the author or contributor
  • Represent work that has actually been published

Examples of acceptable published work include:

  • Reported articles
  • Policy analyses
  • Issue analyses
  • Opinion articles
  • Essays
  • Podcasts
  • Newsletters
  • Data projects

However, social media posts are not considered published work for this application.

Unpublished materials such as class assignments and dissertations are also not accepted.

Applicants who submit translated work may do so, but they must provide at least one submission written in English. Applicants are also expected to demonstrate their own command of English.

If a submitted article is behind a paywall, applicants must ensure that the pieces submitted for consideration are open access.

How Recent Should Your Writing Samples Be?

Writing samples should generally be from the past three years.

Applicants should therefore prioritize recent work that demonstrates their current expertise, writing ability and understanding of their chosen technology policy area.

Can Applicants Submit Co-Authored Work?

Yes. Co-authored publications are permitted.

However, Tech Policy Press recommends that applicants submit at least one solo publication as part of their application.

This gives the selection team an opportunity to assess the applicant’s individual writing and analytical capabilities.

Can Fellows Work Across Multiple Formats?

Yes.

Applicants will not be disadvantaged for being open to working in multiple formats. The fellowship welcomes contributions across different forms of public-interest journalism, analysis and related work, provided that the work aligns with Tech Policy Press’s editorial focus.

Fellowship Application Requirements

Applicants must submit an online application containing the required supporting materials.

The application requires:

  1. Curriculum vitae or resume
  2. Cover letter of no more than two pages
  3. Links to previous publications
  4. Two professional references

What Should the Cover Letter Include?

The cover letter should explain what the applicant hopes to accomplish during the fellowship.

Applicants should use the cover letter to clearly communicate their proposed area of focus and demonstrate why they are well positioned to pursue the work.

A strong application should make it clear what issue the applicant wants to explore and how their work could contribute to public understanding and informed decision-making.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship is:

September 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

Applicants should complete and submit the online application before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the official Tech Policy Press application form.

Applicants should prepare their resume or CV, cover letter, publication links and two professional references before beginning the application.

Application: https://airtable.com/appfRgsTRubbZBBPq/pagINFzaysYPJ2qJ3/form

Information Sessions for Applicants

Tech Policy Press will host two online information sessions for people considering applying.

Registration is required.

Information Session 1

Date: September 9, 2026
Time: 8:00 a.m. EDT
Platform: Zoom

Information Session 2

Date: September 16, 2026
Time: 7:00 p.m. EDT
Platform: Zoom

Applicants can choose whichever session is more convenient.

The sessions provide an opportunity for potential applicants to learn more about the fellowship before submitting their applications.

Visit HERE to learn more about the 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship

When Will Selected Fellows Be Notified?

Tech Policy Press aims to notify applicants about their application status by early December 2026.

A selected pool of applicants may also be invited to participate in an online interview as part of the selection process.

When Does the Fellowship Begin?

The 2027 fellowship is scheduled to begin in January 2027.

The program will run for 12 months, meaning the fellowship will continue throughout 2027.

The fellowship is part-time, allowing participants to continue engaging with their professional work while contributing to their fellowship responsibilities.

Are Monthly Submissions Exclusive?

Yes.

Monthly submissions are expected to be exclusive to Tech Policy Press, although fellows may republish their work afterward.

This arrangement allows Tech Policy Press to publish and showcase fellows’ work while still giving fellows the ability to distribute their work more broadly after publication.

How Tech Policy Press Supports Fellows’ Work

Beyond the stipend and editorial guidance, the program provides an environment designed to help fellows develop their work and professional networks.

Participants can benefit from:

  • An international network of current and past fellows
  • Regular feedback and exchange of ideas
  • Editorial support
  • Monthly learning opportunities
  • Opportunities to develop sources within their focus area
  • Publication opportunities through Tech Policy Press
  • Potential exposure through the organization’s newsletter
  • Potential podcast and event opportunities
  • A structured year-long environment for producing public-interest work

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Technology Policy Professionals

Technology is increasingly connected to questions surrounding democracy, governance, rights, public policy and society. This fellowship provides an opportunity for experienced professionals to dedicate a year to examining these issues through reporting and analysis.

The combination of a $10,000 stipend, editorial support, international networking, publication opportunities and a structured 12-month program makes the fellowship particularly relevant to professionals looking to expand their body of work in technology policy.

It can also provide a platform for people who want to bring greater attention to technology policy issues affecting communities and regions that are often underrepresented in global discussions.

Conclusion

The 2027 Tech Policy Press Fellowship offers journalists, researchers, lawyers and public policy professionals an opportunity to spend a year developing independent reporting and analysis on important questions surrounding technology and democracy.

Selected fellows will receive a $10,000 stipend, participate in an international cohort, receive ongoing editorial guidance and have opportunities to publish and showcase their work through Tech Policy Press.

The fellowship is part-time, remote and open to applicants worldwide, making it accessible to professionals both inside and outside the United States.

Those interested in applying should begin preparing their CV or resume, two-page cover letter, recent published work and two professional references well before the deadline.

Application deadline: September 24, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. EDT.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.
