item.content:encoded:
Submissions are open for the International Physics Competition 2026, also known as IPhyC 2026. Officially described as the “Education Program & Talent Search in Physics,” IPhyC is an international online initiative that allows participants to test their physics knowledge, strengthen their scientific reasoning and engage with problems extending beyond the conventional classroom curriculum.

The competition is conducted online, meaning participants can enter without travelling to another country or attending an in-person international event. It combines accessible introductory problems with advanced calculations, research-based questions and fast-paced assessments across three progressive rounds.

The Qualification Round is free to enter. Participants must download the official problem sheet, solve the questions and submit their work online by Sunday, 1 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0. Successful participants can progress to the Semi-Final and Final rounds, where they may compete for cash prizes, international honours, national awards and verifiable certificates.

What Is the International Physics Competition?

The International Physics Competition is an independent educational programme designed to make international physics challenges accessible through digital technology. It is coordinated by Edu.Harbour and brings together participants, teachers, schools and local representatives from different parts of the world.

Its purpose goes beyond ranking competitors. IPhyC aims to encourage curiosity about physics, introduce participants to unconventional problem formats and help them develop skills that can support future studies in science, technology, engineering and research.

According to the organizers, the programme is intended to supplement established national and international physics Olympiads rather than replace them. Its focus is broader accessibility, educational development and exposure to scientific research. Read more about IPhyC’s mission and structure.

International Physics Competition 2026 at a Glance

Item Details
Programme name International Physics Competition 2026
Official subtitle Education Program & Talent Search in Physics
Competition format Three online rounds
Qualification Round fee Free
Semi-Final Round fee EUR 12 for qualified participants
Qualification deadline Sunday, 1 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0
Qualification results Monday, 16 November 2026
Semi-Final examination window 13–15 December 2026
Final Round date Tuesday, 12 January 2027
Final results Monday, 18 January 2027
Published award-package value USD 1,500
Highest individual cash prize USD 250
Participation mode Primarily online
Official website International Physics Competition
Submission portal Submit a Qualification Round solution

Why Participate in IPhyC 2026?

IPhyC provides an opportunity to apply theoretical physics knowledge to diverse and unfamiliar problems. Participants are expected to combine calculations, logical reasoning, reading comprehension and scientific interpretation.

The principal features include:

  • A globally accessible online format.
  • The same problems for participants around the world.
  • Separate age and academic groups with adjusted qualifying scores.
  • A free Qualification Round.
  • Research-based problems connected to real scientific publications.
  • A structured pathway from an open Qualification Round to supervised examinations.
  • Participation certificates for all valid participants.
  • Cash prizes and special certificates for leading finalists.
  • National awards for strong performers from individual countries.
  • Online accounts through which participants can access results, performance reports and certificates.
  • Resources for teachers, schools and local physics groups.
  • An alumni network through which former participants may receive information about scholarships, sponsored events and other academic opportunities.

Academic Areas Covered by IPhyC

The competition can draw on a wide range of theoretical and applied physics subjects. The official website’s learning and preparation resources cover areas such as:

  • Mechanics
  • Electrodynamics
  • Thermodynamics
  • Quantum mechanics
  • Relativity
  • Fluid dynamics
  • Optics
  • Particle physics
  • Solid-state physics
  • Plasma physics
  • Astrophysics

Participants should not assume that every topic will appear in every round. Instead, they should prepare broadly and practise applying fundamental principles in unfamiliar contexts.

IPhyC is designed to develop several transferable academic skills:

  • Logical reasoning and creative problem-solving
  • Knowledge of physical laws, concepts and definitions
  • Mathematical calculation
  • Scientific reading comprehension
  • Analytical thinking
  • Application of theoretical knowledge
  • Time management
  • Adaptability to different question formats
  • Clear presentation of scientific solutions

The official IPhyC training and preparation page provides preparation advice, recommended reading and previous competition material.

How the International Physics Competition 2026 Works

The competition consists of three stages:

  1. Qualification Round
  2. Semi-Final Round
  3. Final Round

Participants must achieve the prescribed score for their age group before progressing to the next stage.

Stage One: Qualification Round

The Qualification Round is the open-entry stage of IPhyC 2026. It contains five physics problems identified as Problems A, B, C, D and E.

The problems vary in subject, difficulty and format. Some primarily assess physics knowledge, while others require mathematical calculations, interpretation and structured reasoning.

Qualification Round scoring

Each of the five problems carries a maximum of five points, creating a total possible score of 25 points.

The minimum scores required to advance are:

Group Minimum qualifying score
Junior 15 out of 25
Youth 17 out of 25
Senior 20 out of 25

All groups receive the same problems, but the qualifying threshold increases for the more advanced groups.

Qualification Round deadline

The final submission deadline is:

Sunday, 1 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0

The organizers recommend submitting earlier to avoid last-minute internet, file-upload or website-related problems.

Submission format

Solutions may be:

  • Professionally typed using a computer programme such as TeX;
  • Typed using another word-processing programme and converted to PDF; or
  • Written by hand and uploaded as clear scanned images or photographs.

Digitally typeset solutions may receive a special honorary note on the participant’s certificate.

Only one solution file may be uploaded. If a participant has several images, they must be combined into one PDF before submission.

Accepted formats are:

  • PDF
  • JPG
  • JPEG
  • PNG

The following formats are not accepted:

  • DOC
  • DOCX
  • ZIP
  • Other unsupported file types

The uploaded file must be smaller than 10 MB.

Qualification Round participation cost

There is no registration charge for the Qualification Round. A valid solution must, however, be submitted; incomplete registrations without an attached solution may be deleted.

Announcement of results

Qualification Round results are scheduled to be announced on Monday, 16 November 2026.

Participants should receive the result by email. They can also log in to their participant accounts to access:

  • Their competition status;
  • Results;
  • Performance reports;
  • Certificates; and
  • Information about the next round.

Stage Two: Semi-Final Round

Participants who meet the Qualification Round threshold may register for the Semi-Final Round.

The current 2026 round structure consists of a supervised 60-minute examination with three problems:

Problem Maximum points Description
Basic problem 4 A comparatively approachable physics question
Advanced problem 6 A more challenging analytical problem
Research problem 8 A question connected to a real scientific research paper

The maximum available score is 18 points.

Semi-Final qualifying scores

Group Score needed for Final Round
Junior 9 out of 18
Youth 11 out of 18
Senior 13 out of 18

Research-paper preparation

The research paper for the Semi-Final Round is scheduled to be released on Friday, 11 December 2026.

Qualified and registered participants will receive it through email and their participant accounts. Participants may use translation tools and artificial intelligence tools during the preparation period to help them understand the research paper.

However, these tools cannot be used to obtain assistance during the supervised examination itself.

Semi-Final examination period

The examination can be taken at any selected time during the following window:

  • Opening: Sunday, 13 December 2026 at 00:01 UTC+0
  • Closing: Tuesday, 15 December 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0

Once started, the participant has 60 minutes to complete the examination. After the examination ends, a further 10 minutes is provided to scan and upload the written answers. This upload period remains supervised.

Supervision options

Participants have two supervision options.

Option One: Teacher supervision

Teacher supervision is recommended. The supervising teacher must:

  • Be employed by a government-accredited school or university;
  • Be an active teacher or professor rather than retired;
  • Not be related to the participant;
  • Register with IPhyC; and
  • Receive approval before supervising the examination.

The teacher must also document the examination conditions as required by the organizers.

Option Two: Online supervision

Participants without an eligible teacher may use IPhyC’s online supervision system. This requires:

  • A computer, laptop or phone with a webcam as the examination device;
  • A separate phone with a camera and microphone as the supervision device;
  • A valid government-issued identity card or passport;
  • A stable internet connection; and
  • An appropriate private examination environment.

Semi-Final registration cost

Qualified participants who choose to enter the Semi-Final Round must pay EUR 12. The general rules describe this payment as non-refundable.

The Semi-Final registration deadline is Tuesday, 8 December 2026.

Semi-Final results are expected on Monday, 28 December 2026. Complete information is available on the official 2026 Process and Rounds page.

Financial Aid for Semi-Finalists

IPhyC offers limited financial assistance for qualified participants who cannot afford the EUR 12 Semi-Final fee.

Two forms of assistance are available:

  • A 50% reduction in the registration fee; or
  • A complete fee waiver.

Financial aid is limited and depends on sponsorship funding. Receiving support is therefore not guaranteed.

Applicants must generally submit:

  • A written explanation of their financial circumstances; and
  • Evidence of household income, such as a salary slip, tax statement or official income certificate.

The financial-aid request deadline is Monday, 23 November 2026. Requests are assessed according to demonstrated financial need and the quality of the applicant’s Qualification Round work. Review the official financial-aid conditions.

Stage Three: Final Round

Participants who achieve the required Semi-Final score progress to the Final Round.

The Final Round is scheduled for:

Tuesday, 12 January 2027

The current 2026 information describes it as a digitally monitored online examination with approximately 30 questions. It takes around 30 minutes and may contain:

  • Multiple-choice questions;
  • Short-answer questions;
  • Questions connected to previous rounds;
  • Questions requiring knowledge from different branches of physics; and
  • Problems related to the Semi-Final research material.

Final rankings are determined primarily by performance in the Final Round. If two or more participants obtain the same Final Round score, Semi-Final and Qualification Round scores may be used as tie-breakers.

Final Round results are scheduled for Monday, 18 January 2027.

Complete IPhyC 2026 Timeline

Activity Date
Qualification Round submission deadline 1 November 2026, 23:59 UTC+0
Qualification Round results 16 November 2026
Financial-aid request deadline 23 November 2026
Semi-Final registration deadline 8 December 2026
Research paper released 11 December 2026
Semi-Final examination window 13–15 December 2026
Semi-Final results 28 December 2026
Final Round examination 12 January 2027
Final results 18 January 2027

Applicants should monitor the official website and their email accounts because the organizers reserve the right to amend dates or procedures when operational circumstances require changes.

Cash Prizes and International Awards

The official awards page describes the complete IPhyC 2026 award package as being worth USD 1,500, including cash prizes and special honours.

The published individual cash-prize schedule is:

Group Position Cash prize
Senior First Prize USD 250
Senior Second Prize USD 175
Senior Third Prize USD 125
Youth First Prize USD 200
Youth Second Prize USD 150
Youth Third Prize USD 100
Junior First Prize USD 175
Junior Second Prize USD 125
Junior Third Prize USD 100

The nine listed cash payments total USD 1,400. The official USD 1,500 description refers to the broader award package, including special honours and certificates, rather than USD 1,500 in itemized cash payments.

First-, second- and third-prize winners also receive special prize certificates. The organizers state that hard copies are sent to these leading prize winners, while other participants receive digital certificates containing permanent verification identification numbers. View the official prize schedule.

Certificates, Honours and National Recognition

Recognition is not limited to the nine cash-prize winners.

The awards structure includes:

  • Official participation certificates for valid participants;
  • Semi-Finalist certificates;
  • Bronze, Silver or Gold honours for Finalists, depending on performance;
  • Special certificates for first-, second- and third-prize winners;
  • National Award certificates; and
  • A special honorary note for professionally typeset Qualification Round solutions.

The top three participants from a country may receive National Awards if they obtain at least 50% of the available Final Round points. The organizers may also publish a list of leading national performers.

Certificates include verification codes that allow schools, universities and other institutions to confirm their authenticity through the IPhyC website.

Information Required for Submission

Applicants should prepare the following information before opening the submission form:

  • Correct full name;
  • Date of birth;
  • Current country and city of study;
  • Active email address;
  • A password containing at least eight characters;
  • Official name of the school or university;
  • Grade or university year applicable on 1 November 2026;
  • Completed Qualification Round solution file;
  • Teacher or school email address, if available;
  • Preferred communication language; and
  • Local IPhyC representative’s name, if applicable.

The teacher’s email address and local representative selection are optional.

Participants must enter their names and dates of birth accurately because these details are used on certificates. The organizers may verify the ages of prize winners.

How to Enter the International Physics Competition 2026

Follow these steps:

  1. Visit the official IPhyC website.
  2. Download the 2026 Qualification Round problem sheet.
  3. Review all five problems carefully.
  4. Solve as many problems as possible and show the reasoning behind each answer.
  5. Type the solutions or prepare clear scans of handwritten work.
  6. Combine everything into one accepted file.
  7. Ensure that the file is smaller than 10 MB.
  8. Open the official submission form.
  9. Enter the required personal and academic details accurately.
  10. Upload the solution file.
  11. Read and accept the competition rules and data policy.
  12. Submit before 1 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0.
  13. Monitor the registered email address and participant account for confirmation and results.

Submissions are not accepted by email.

Collaboration, Academic Integrity and Cheating Rules

Every participant must submit an individual solution.

During the Qualification Round, participants may:

  • Work with classmates or friends to explore possible approaches;
  • Receive basic guidance from a teacher;
  • Consult books and online material for general definitions and scientific background; and
  • Discuss the underlying concepts.

They may not:

  • Copy another person’s exact solution;
  • Copy a completed solution from the internet;
  • Ask users on an online platform to solve the problems for them; or
  • Submit work that is not their own.

During the Semi-Final examination, participants cannot use external websites, books, notes or assistance from another person. A calculator is permitted in the Semi-Final Round, but artificial intelligence and translation tools are limited to understanding the research paper during the preparation period.

During the Final Round, calculators, external sources and assistance from others are prohibited. Only blank paper and a pencil may be used for notes.

Cheating, plagiarism, impersonation or the submission of falsified information can result in immediate disqualification and loss of any registration fee. Participants should read the complete IPhyC cheating policy before entering.

How to Prepare for IPhyC 2026

A strong preparation strategy should include the following:

1. Understand the three-round structure

The Qualification Round rewards complete reasoning and clear written solutions. The Semi-Final adds a supervised, time-limited research component, while the Final requires faster responses across different physics fields.

2. Review fundamental physics

Focus on essential principles in mechanics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, optics, modern physics, fluids and related topics.

3. Practise presenting complete solutions

Do not provide only a numerical answer. Define the variables, identify the relevant physical law, show the calculations and state the final result clearly with the correct units.

4. Strengthen scientific reading skills

Practise reading research abstracts, identifying a paper’s main finding and connecting unfamiliar terminology to familiar physics principles.

5. Solve problems under time limits

Timed practice is particularly important for the supervised Semi-Final and fast-paced Final Round.

6. Learn from errors

After attempting a problem, compare the approach with an official or trusted solution. Identify whether the mistake came from conceptual understanding, algebra, units, interpretation or time management.

7. Use official preparation materials

Consult previous IPhyC problems, recommended textbooks and the resources available through the official training page.

Role of Teachers and Schools

Teachers are not required for the initial Qualification Round, but they can play a valuable role in sharing the competition, guiding students and supervising later stages.

Registered teachers may be able to:

  • View their students’ results and certificates;
  • Download teacher reports;
  • Pay Semi-Final fees for multiple students as a group;
  • Supervise Semi-Final examinations; and
  • Access educational materials.

IPhyC also offers honorary awards for teachers and schools with significant participation, strong student performance or notable contributions. These awards do not include cash payments.

Language and Global Accessibility

English is the original language of IPhyC. The website also provides translated interfaces in German, Arabic, Chinese, French, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Portuguese, Vietnamese, Japanese, Korean and Turkish.

The organizers indicate that non-English versions may contain automatic translations. Participants using a translated version should therefore compare any uncertain scientific wording with the original English material.

Because the competition is mainly online, no international travel is required. Participants should nevertheless ensure that they have reliable internet access and the necessary devices before any supervised examination.

Important Points to Remember

  • The Qualification Round is free, but the Semi-Final costs EUR 12.
  • Limited financial aid is available for eligible Semi-Finalists.
  • The Qualification Round deadline is 1 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0.
  • One solution file must be uploaded in an accepted format.
  • The file must be under 10 MB.
  • The same problems are given to all age groups.
  • Older groups have higher qualifying thresholds.
  • Personal information must be entered accurately for certificates.
  • All entries are individual, even where limited Qualification Round discussion is allowed.
  • Applicants should rely on the official website for any timetable changes.

Conclusion

The International Physics Competition 2026 offers an accessible way to test physics knowledge in an international setting without the cost and logistical burden of travelling overseas. Its three-round structure combines open-ended problem-solving, engagement with scientific research and supervised online assessments.

Participants can earn internationally verifiable certificates, compete for cash prizes and national recognition, and develop practical skills in scientific reasoning, analytical thinking and research comprehension. Anyone planning to enter should download the Qualification Round problem sheet immediately, prepare a complete and clearly presented solution, and submit well before the official deadline of 1 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC+0.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Youth Office is inviting young people from diverse backgrounds to apply for participation in the 2026 UN Youth Townhall, a flagship youth engagement gathering taking place in Heidelberg, Germany, from 8 to 10 December 2026.

The Townhall is designed to bring young people together with governments, the United Nations, civil society, the private sector and other partners to move beyond dialogue and develop concrete recommendations, partnerships and opportunities for action.

For the 2026 gathering, the UN Youth Office will support a limited number of eligible young people aged 18 to 35 to participate in person. The selection process aims to promote diversity, including geographical representation, gender balance and participation from underrepresented and marginalized youth.

The application deadline is 7 September 2026 at midnight ET.

2026 UN Youth Townhall at a Glance

Opportunity detail Information
Opportunity 2026 UN Youth Townhall
Organizer UN Youth Office with support from partners
Location Heidelberg, Germany
Dates 8–10 December 2026
Eligible age 18–35 years
Participation In-person
Number supported Limited number of young people
Application deadline 7 September 2026, midnight ET
Application time Approximately 30–45 minutes
Selection notification Successful applicants will be notified; if no notification is received by 8 October 2026, applicants are encouraged to explore other opportunities
Application guidance Official UN Youth Townhall application guidance
Application platform Microsoft Forms

What Is the 2026 UN Youth Townhall?

The 2026 UN Youth Townhall is described as the first convening of its kind and is a flagship gathering of the UN Youth Compass.

The event is intended to create a space where young people can engage meaningfully with decision-makers and other important stakeholders on issues affecting young people and the wider world.

Rather than limiting youth participation to discussion and consultation, the Townhall aims to generate tangible outcomes.

These include:

  • Concrete recommendations;
  • Partnerships;
  • Opportunities for action;
  • Continued engagement between young people and institutions; and
  • Stronger connections between youth and decision-makers.

The Townhall will bring together young people from diverse backgrounds with representatives from governments, the United Nations, civil society, the private sector and other partners.

This makes the event particularly relevant to young people interested in youth participation, international development, policymaking, peace and security, sustainable development, human rights and global affairs.

Where and When Will the UN Youth Townhall Take Place?

The 2026 UN Youth Townhall will take place in:

Heidelberg, Germany

The event is scheduled for:

8–10 December 2026

Selected young participants will therefore need to be available to participate in person during the Townhall dates.

The source specifically states that the UN Youth Office will support a limited number of young people to participate in person.

Who Is the UN Youth Townhall Looking For?

The open call is aimed at young people between the ages of 18 and 35.

However, age alone does not determine selection.

The UN Youth Office states that the selection process will consider several factors to help ensure meaningful and diverse youth representation.

These include:

  • Gender balance;
  • Geographical representation;
  • Participation of youth from underrepresented groups;
  • Participation of youth from marginalized groups;
  • Engagement with grassroots organizations; and
  • Previous engagement with the United Nations.

The selection process will be conducted by the UN Youth Office, with support from online volunteers and the Youth Advisory Group to the UN Youth Townhall.

Preference for Grassroots Youth Engagement

One particularly important aspect of the call is the preference given to young people who are engaged in grassroots organizations.

The UN Youth Office also indicates that preference will be given to applicants who have had limited or no prior engagement with the United Nations.

This is significant because the Townhall is designed to broaden youth participation rather than simply bring together young people who already have extensive experience within international institutions.

Young people who are actively contributing to their communities through grassroots initiatives may therefore find this opportunity particularly relevant.

Representation of Underrepresented and Marginalized Youth

The UN Youth Office aims to ensure that the Townhall reflects the diversity of young people.

The selection process will therefore consider participation from underrepresented and marginalized groups.

The application form specifically asks applicants whether they belong to or identify with particular rights-holder communities, including:

  • LGBTQIA+ communities;
  • Indigenous communities;
  • Migrants and internally displaced people;
  • Persons with disabilities;
  • Youth facing work- and descent-based discrimination;
  • Young people living with HIV; and
  • Refugees.

Applicants are given the opportunity to identify with these communities in the application.

The form also asks applicants with disabilities whether they require reasonable accommodation to participate.

Why the UN Youth Townhall Matters

The Townhall is designed around the principle that young people should have meaningful opportunities to contribute to discussions and decisions affecting their lives and communities.

The event is anchored in several major United Nations youth and international policy frameworks.

These include the:

  • UN Youth Compass;
  • UN Secretary-General’s 2023 Policy Brief on Meaningful Youth Engagement;
  • Youth2030: The UN Youth Strategy;
  • Pact for the Future;
  • UN Security Council Resolution 2250 (2015) on Youth, Peace and Security; and
  • UN Security Council Resolution 2807 (2025) on Youth, Peace and Security.

These frameworks provide the broader policy context for the Townhall.

The event therefore represents an opportunity for young participants to engage with international youth policy and contribute perspectives that can inform recommendations and future action.

What Can Participants Expect From the Townhall?

The source emphasizes that the Townhall will go beyond dialogue.

Participants will have an opportunity to connect with a range of stakeholders, including:

Governments

Young participants can engage with government representatives and contribute youth perspectives to policy discussions.

United Nations

The Townhall provides an opportunity for youth to interact with UN representatives and contribute to the organization’s broader youth engagement efforts.

Civil Society

Civil society organizations play an important role in youth participation and community action. The Townhall will provide opportunities for young people to connect with civil society actors.

Private Sector

The event will also connect young people with private-sector stakeholders, creating potential opportunities for collaboration and partnerships.

Other Partners

The gathering will bring together additional organizations and stakeholders working on youth-related issues.

The resulting connections can potentially extend beyond the three-day event, as the Townhall aims to create opportunities for continued engagement after the gathering.

The UN Youth Townhall Is Designed to Generate Action

A major feature of the event is its emphasis on moving from conversation to action.

Rather than simply asking young people to express their views, the Townhall seeks to produce:

  1. Concrete recommendations that can inform future work;
  2. Partnerships between young people and relevant stakeholders; and
  3. Opportunities for action that can continue beyond the Townhall.

This approach places young people not only in the position of participants but also as contributors to solutions and future initiatives.

Application Eligibility

Applicants should carefully review the official application guidance before submitting their applications.

Based on the supplied call, applicants should meet the following central criteria:

Age

Applicants must be between 18 and 35 years old.

Participation

Selected applicants are expected to participate in person at the Townhall in Heidelberg, Germany.

Language

The application asks whether applicants have a working knowledge of English.

Applicants are also asked whether they would require interpretation support and, if so, which language and what scope of support would be required.

Youth Engagement

The opportunity is intended for young people who can contribute meaningfully to the Townhall and its objectives.

The selection process considers the diversity of youth representation and gives preference to young people involved in grassroots organizations.

Important Restriction for Current UN Contractors

There is an important eligibility consideration that applicants should not overlook.

The UN Youth Office states that it is unable to sponsor youth who are currently under contract with the United Nations.

Applicants who are currently working under a UN contract should therefore carefully consider this restriction before applying.

What Information Does the Application Form Request?

The application form contains several sections designed to help the UN Youth Office understand applicants’ backgrounds, circumstances and participation needs.

Personal Information

Applicants are asked to provide basic personal information, including:

  • First name;
  • Last name;
  • Date of birth;
  • Gender identity;
  • Email address;
  • Country of nationality;
  • Country of residence; and
  • City of residence.

The form states that personal information collected in this section will not be disclosed to third parties.

Gender Identity

Applicants are asked about their gender identity.

The options displayed in the form include:

  • Woman;
  • Man;
  • Non-binary; and
  • Prefer not to say.

This information forms part of the application process and can contribute to the organizers’ consideration of gender balance in participant selection.

Rights-Holder Community Information

Applicants can indicate whether they belong to or identify with any of the rights-holder communities listed in the form.

These include:

  • LGBTQIA+;
  • Indigenous Community;
  • Migrants and Internally Displaced People;
  • Persons with Disability;
  • Youth Facing Work and Descent Based Discrimination;
  • Young People Living with HIV; and
  • Refugees.

Applicants should provide this information according to their circumstances and the options available in the application form.

Applicant Category

The application asks candidates which category they most closely associate with.

The listed options are:

  • Youth-led entity/organisation;
  • Youth-serving entity/organisation; or
  • Individual young person aged 35 and below.

This allows the organizers to understand whether an applicant is participating as an individual or through an organization or entity connected to youth work.

Organization of Affiliation

Applicants are also asked to provide their organization of affiliation, if they have one.

This is particularly relevant to applicants involved in:

  • Youth organizations;
  • Grassroots initiatives;
  • Civil society organizations;
  • Community initiatives; or
  • Other youth-related entities.

Applicants without an organizational affiliation can provide the information requested according to their individual circumstances.

Disability and Reasonable Accommodation

The application asks applicants whether they consider themselves a person with a disability.

If the answer is yes, applicants can specify the reasonable accommodation they would need to participate in the UN Youth Townhall.

This allows the organizers to consider accessibility requirements when planning participation.

Applicants who require accommodations should provide sufficient information to help the UN Youth Office understand what support may be needed.

Safety and Security Considerations

The application also provides applicants with an opportunity to identify any safety measures that should be considered to ensure their secure participation in the Townhall.

Examples given in the application include:

  • Avoiding the display of an applicant’s full name;
  • Using a specific travel route; or
  • Other precautions the applicant may require.

This section is particularly relevant for applicants who may have specific safety or privacy concerns connected to their participation.

English Language and Interpretation Support

Applicants are asked whether they have a working knowledge of English.

The form also asks whether selected participants would require interpretation support.

If interpretation is required, applicants can indicate:

  • The language they require; and
  • The scope of interpretation support needed.

This information can help organizers plan appropriate support for participants.

How Long Does the Application Take?

The UN Youth Office estimates that completing the application will take approximately:

30–45 minutes

Applicants should therefore avoid beginning the application immediately before the deadline.

It is advisable to set aside sufficient uninterrupted time to read the questions carefully and provide thoughtful responses.

Application Deadline for the 2026 UN Youth Townhall

The application deadline is:

7 September 2026 at midnight ET.

Applications should be submitted before the deadline.

Because the selection process is expected to attract a large number of applications, prospective participants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit.

When Will Applicants Be Notified?

The UN Youth Office states that, due to the anticipated large number of applications, it will only be able to notify successful applicants.

Applicants who do not receive communication from the office by:

8 October 2026

are encouraged to explore other opportunities.

This means applicants should not necessarily expect an individual rejection notification if they are not selected.

How to Apply for the 2026 UN Youth Townhall

Applicants should first read the Official Application Guidance carefully before completing the form.

Step 1: Review the Application Guidance

The UN Youth Office provides an official application guidance document explaining the call and application process.

Applicants should read this before starting the form.

Step 2: Confirm Your Eligibility

Check that you meet the age requirement and consider the other selection factors and restrictions outlined in the call.

Step 3: Prepare Your Information

Have your basic personal, nationality, residence and organizational information available.

You should also consider in advance whether you need:

  • Reasonable accommodation;
  • Interpretation;
  • Specific safety measures; or
  • Other participation support.

Step 4: Complete the Application Form

The application is submitted through the online form provided by the UN Youth Office.

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Ensure that the completed application is submitted by:

7 September 2026 at midnight ET.

Applicants should allow enough time for any technical issues and for reviewing their responses before submission.

APPLY HERE

Application Guidance

Before applying, applicants should read the official guidance document:

UN Youth Townhall Sponsored Youth Engagement Application Guidance

The guidance should be treated as an important reference when preparing the application.

Youth2030 and Continued Engagement

The UN Youth Townhall is connected to the wider Youth2030 framework and the UN’s efforts to strengthen meaningful youth participation.

Participants will not simply be brought together for a single event. The Townhall aims to create opportunities for continued engagement beyond the gathering.

This means the value of participation can extend beyond the three days in Heidelberg.

Young people can potentially use the experience to:

  • Strengthen connections with other youth leaders;
  • Develop relationships with institutions;
  • Exchange ideas across countries and regions;
  • Contribute to recommendations;
  • Explore potential partnerships; and
  • Remain engaged in youth-related international processes.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to young people who are:

  • Between 18 and 35 years old;
  • Active in youth-led or youth-serving organizations;
  • Working with grassroots communities;
  • Interested in youth participation;
  • Engaged in social or community initiatives;
  • Interested in international development;
  • Interested in peace and security;
  • Working on issues affecting marginalized or underrepresented communities;
  • Interested in connecting with policymakers and international organizations; or
  • Looking for meaningful opportunities to contribute to global youth policy discussions.

The call does not suggest that applicants must have previously participated in UN programmes. In fact, limited or no previous UN engagement is identified as a preference.

How to Strengthen Your Application

While selection is competitive, applicants can improve the quality of their submission by approaching the application thoughtfully.

Demonstrate Meaningful Youth Engagement

Explain clearly how you engage with young people, your community or an issue affecting youth.

Highlight Grassroots Experience

If you are involved in a grassroots organization or community initiative, clearly explain your role and the impact of your work.

Explain Your Perspective

The Townhall seeks diverse youth representation. Applicants should clearly communicate the perspectives, experiences and issues they can contribute to the gathering.

Be Clear About Accessibility Needs

If you require reasonable accommodation, interpretation or specific safety measures, provide the relevant information in the appropriate section of the application.

Review Before Submitting

Because the application takes approximately 30–45 minutes, applicants should reserve enough time to review their answers carefully before submission.

APPLY HERE

A Global Youth Participation Opportunity

The 2026 UN Youth Townhall is structured to bring together young people from diverse geographical and social backgrounds.

Geographical representation is specifically included among the selection considerations.

The call does not identify a restricted list of eligible countries in the supplied information. Applicants are therefore encouraged to review the official application guidance and form carefully to determine whether they meet all requirements.

The opportunity should not be viewed as being limited to one continent or region.

Visit HERE to learn more about the UN Youth Townhall in Germany.

Conclusion

The 2026 UN Youth Townhall in Heidelberg, Germany provides young people aged 18–35 with an opportunity to participate in a major United Nations youth engagement gathering focused on turning youth dialogue into recommendations, partnerships and action.

Taking place from 8–10 December 2026, the Townhall will connect young people with governments, the United Nations, civil society, the private sector and other partners.

The UN Youth Office intends to support a limited number of young people to participate in person, with selection considering gender balance, geographical representation and participation from underrepresented and marginalized groups. Preference will also be given to young people involved in grassroots organizations and those with limited or no previous engagement with the United Nations.

The application deadline is 7 September 2026 at midnight ET, and applicants should expect the form to take approximately 30–45 minutes to complete.

Prospective applicants should carefully review the official application guidance, confirm their eligibility, prepare the requested personal and participation information, and submit their application well before the deadline.

For young people seeking to contribute to international youth policy, connect with decision-makers, share community perspectives and participate in meaningful global youth engagement, the 2026 UN Youth Townhall represents an opportunity to make their voices heard at an important international gathering.

Discover more global Conference and UN opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) is inviting applications for its International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship (DPHD) for international students who will commence or continue a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in 2027.

The scholarship provides successful applicants with a tax-free stipend of AUD $39,000 per year as well as coverage of tuition fees for up to three years of full-time equivalent PhD study.

Applications are welcomed across all research areas, provided the proposed research aligns with one of UniSQ’s flagship research areas. The scholarship is designed to support high-achieving international researchers who demonstrate strong academic performance, research capability, and a well-developed research proposal.

About the UniSQ International PhD Scholarship

The International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship is a competitive research scholarship for international students pursuing doctoral research at UniSQ.

The scholarship combines the stipend and tuition-fee components into one application. Applicants do not need to apply separately for the stipend and tuition-fee scholarship.

Successful scholars will have the opportunity to undertake doctoral research within UniSQ’s research environment while receiving financial support for their studies.

Applicants are encouraged to explore UniSQ’s available research thesis topics and identify potential supervisors whose expertise aligns with their proposed research.

Scholarship Benefits

The UniSQ scholarship provides substantial financial support throughout the doctoral programme.

AUD $39,000 Annual Stipend

Successful applicants will receive a stipend of:

AUD $39,000 per annum

This financial support is intended to assist scholars with living and study-related expenses while undertaking their PhD.

Full Tuition Fee Support

UniSQ will pay tuition fees for a maximum period of:

Three years of full-time equivalent study

The scholarship covers the applicable tuition fees during the supported period.

However, any period of study already undertaken towards the PhD will be deducted from the scholarship period.

Research Areas

Applications are welcomed across different areas of research, but proposed projects must align with UniSQ’s flagship research areas.

Applicants should discuss the flagship area that most closely matches their proposed research with their potential supervisor before submitting their application.

This alignment is important because applicants are assessed partly on the relationship between their proposed research and UniSQ’s research priorities.

Prospective applicants can also explore UniSQ’s current research thesis topics and connect with UniSQ experts to identify appropriate research opportunities and potential supervisory arrangements.

Industry Stream

The scholarship also provides an optional Industry Stream.

The Industry Stream is designed to create stronger connections between doctoral research and industry by requiring successful participants to complete a:

60-day industry internship

Applicants interested in this stream are responsible for identifying an appropriate industry partner, either independently or with support from their prospective supervisor.

The industry partner must complete a Letter of Support as part of the application.

If the scholarship is awarded under the Industry Stream, all required contractual agreements must be completed before the student begins the programme.

Continuing Student Requirements for the Industry Stream

Continuing students applying for the Industry Stream must meet additional timing requirements.

They must be:

  • Within 18 months of commencing full-time study, or
  • Within 36 months of commencing part-time study.

Applicants are advised to consult UniSQ’s Senior Coordinator for Commercialisation and Partnerships before applying to ensure that the proposed internship meets the university’s requirements.

Dedicated Opportunities for Women in STEMM and Students With Disabilities

In addition to the Industry Stream, the scholarship offering includes dedicated scholarships for:

  • Women in STEMM
  • Students with disabilities

This provides additional opportunities for applicants from groups specifically supported through UniSQ’s research scholarship offerings.

Applicants should review the relevant scholarship requirements when preparing their application.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the UniSQ International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship, applicants must meet the university’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

Hold the Required Academic Qualification

Applicants must have completed a Bachelor Degree with First Class Honours, or an equivalent qualification.

Applicants should provide evidence of their academic qualifications and transcripts as part of the application.

Be Eligible for Full-Time PhD Study

Applicants must be eligible to enrol full-time and on-campus in the Doctor of Philosophy programme at UniSQ.

The scholarship is therefore intended for students who satisfy the university’s requirements for admission to its PhD programme.

Be an International Student

Applicants must be international students.

They must not be:

  • Australian citizens
  • New Zealand citizens
  • Australian permanent residents

Commence or Continue Study in 2027

Applicants must either:

  • Commence their PhD studies in 2027, or
  • Continue their existing PhD studies in 2027.

Academic and Research Selection Criteria

Eligibility does not automatically guarantee a scholarship.

Applications are assessed using several selection criteria designed to identify applicants with strong academic and research potential.

Academic Achievement

The university considers applicants’ academic records, including:

  • Honours classification or equivalent
  • Performance in postgraduate study
  • Academic prizes
  • Academic awards
  • Overall academic achievement

Applicants with a strong academic history are therefore likely to be more competitive.

Research Capability

Applicants are also assessed on evidence of their ability to conduct high-quality research.

Relevant evidence may include:

  • Research publications in high-quality journals
  • Conference presentations
  • Research internship experience
  • Creative works, where applicable
  • Other evidence demonstrating research capability

Applicants should clearly demonstrate their previous research experience and achievements.

Research Project and Environment

The proposed PhD project is another important part of the assessment.

The university may consider:

  • Alignment with UniSQ research priorities
  • Relevance to the Australian research context
  • External support for the proposed research
  • Potential impact of the research
  • Resources required to successfully complete the research

Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal is clear, realistic, relevant, and well aligned with UniSQ’s research strengths.

Supervisory Team

The proposed supervisory team is also considered.

Applicants are encouraged to work closely with prospective supervisors and demonstrate:

  • The supervisors’ publication records
  • Complementary research expertise
  • Supervisor capacity
  • Available resources to support the proposed research

Finding an appropriate supervisor before applying can therefore be an important part of preparing a competitive application.

PhD Admission Is a Separate Process

An important requirement is that applying for the scholarship and applying for admission to the PhD programme are separate processes.

Applicants must begin the application process for admission into the Doctor of Philosophy programme in order to be eligible for the scholarship.

Prospective students should therefore allow sufficient time to complete both processes.

Required Application Documents

Applicants should prepare digital copies of the required supporting documents before beginning the scholarship application.

These include:

  • Statement of Claim completed by the student and supervisor
  • Curriculum vitae, including research publications and/or presentations
  • Preliminary Research Thesis Topic Proposal
  • Documentation confirming citizenship
  • Testamurs and academic transcripts for all undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications

Applicants applying through the Industry Stream must also provide:

  • Letter of Support completed by the industry partner

All documents should be prepared carefully and submitted according to UniSQ’s application requirements.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow the university’s application process.

Step 1: Identify Your Research Area

Review UniSQ’s flagship research areas and identify the area that most closely aligns with your proposed PhD research.

Step 2: Find a Potential Supervisor

Applicants should connect with a potential supervisor whose research expertise matches their proposed project.

Discussing the proposed research with the supervisor can help applicants refine their research direction and identify the appropriate UniSQ flagship area.

Step 3: Begin the PhD Admission Process

Applicants must start the separate application process for admission to the Doctor of Philosophy programme.

Step 4: Prepare the Scholarship Documents

Prepare the required academic records, CV, research proposal, Statement of Claim, citizenship documentation, and other supporting materials.

Step 5: Submit the Scholarship Application

The scholarship application must be submitted through the UniSQ Scholarship Application Management System before the closing date.

Application Portal: https://scholarships-apply.usq.edu.au/

Applicants who need assistance can consult the university’s Scholarship Online Application Manual.

Application Deadline

The closing date for the scholarship is:

27 September 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and allow enough time to obtain supporting documents and complete the separate PhD admission process.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for international students who:

  • Have completed a Bachelor’s degree with First Class Honours or equivalent
  • Have strong academic achievements
  • Have research experience or demonstrated research capability
  • Have a clear and original PhD research idea
  • Want to pursue doctoral research in Australia
  • Can align their proposed research with a UniSQ flagship area
  • Are able to enrol full-time and on-campus
  • Plan to commence or continue their PhD studies in 2027

Researchers with publications, conference presentations, research internships, or other evidence of research capability may be particularly competitive.

Why Consider the UniSQ Scholarship?

Pursuing a PhD internationally can involve significant tuition and living costs. This scholarship can substantially reduce the financial burden by combining an annual stipend with tuition-fee support.

The AUD $39,000 annual stipend provides financial assistance throughout the supported scholarship period, while UniSQ covers tuition fees for up to three years of full-time equivalent study.

The opportunity also provides access to a research environment where doctoral candidates can work with experienced supervisors and engage with research projects aligned with UniSQ’s flagship areas.

The optional Industry Stream adds another dimension by providing an opportunity for eligible scholarship recipients to undertake a 60-day industry internship.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Applicants should not wait until the final days before the deadline to begin their applications.

Finding a suitable supervisor, developing a research proposal, obtaining academic documents, and completing the separate PhD admission process can require considerable preparation.

Applicants should also ensure that their proposed research is genuinely aligned with UniSQ’s research priorities and that they can clearly explain the expected contribution and impact of their project.

For the Industry Stream, applicants should begin discussions with a potential industry partner early enough to obtain the required Letter of Support and complete any necessary agreements.

Conclusion

The UniSQ International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship 2027 is a significant opportunity for high-achieving international students seeking to undertake PhD research in Australia.

Successful applicants can receive AUD $39,000 per year and tuition-fee coverage for up to three years of full-time equivalent study. The scholarship welcomes research proposals across multiple areas, provided they align with UniSQ’s flagship research priorities.

In addition to the standard scholarship, applicants can explore the optional Industry Stream, which includes a mandatory 60-day industry internship, as well as dedicated opportunities for women in STEMM and students with disabilities.

With a deadline of 27 September 2026, prospective applicants should begin preparing their research proposal, identifying a potential supervisor, gathering supporting documents, and starting the separate PhD admission process well in advance.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Digital Education Council (DEC) Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026 is a new research-focused opportunity designed for postgraduate researchers who are interested in artificial intelligence, digital education, higher education, and emerging issues shaping the future of learning. The fellowship aims to strengthen the Digital Education Council’s global research agenda by bringing talented researchers into its international research activities. Selected fellows will have the opportunity to contribute to the design and delivery of DEC’s global Working Groups while supporting the development of research publications focused on artificial intelligence and other rapidly developing issues in higher education.

With artificial intelligence transforming teaching, learning, assessment, academic research, university administration, and the wider higher education ecosystem, this fellowship provides an opportunity for postgraduate researchers to engage directly with research questions that are increasingly important to universities and education policymakers around the world.

Application Deadline: Monday, 14 September 2026

About the Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026

The Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship is intended to support and expand DEC’s global research activities.

The programme connects postgraduate-level researchers with an international research agenda focused on digital transformation in education. Fellows will work alongside DEC’s broader research activities and contribute to initiatives examining how emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, are influencing higher education.

Rather than being limited to traditional academic research conducted independently, the fellowship is designed around practical engagement with DEC’s global Working Groups and research publications.

This means selected researchers can potentially gain experience in areas such as:

  • Higher education research
  • Artificial intelligence and education
  • Digital transformation
  • Emerging technologies
  • Research publication development
  • International research collaboration
  • Higher education policy and practice
  • Global education trends
  • Research-driven Working Groups

What Will Selected Fellows Do?

Researchers selected for the 2026 Postgraduate Research Fellowship will support two important areas of the Digital Education Council’s work.

1. Support DEC Global Working Groups

One of the key responsibilities of fellows will be to support the design and delivery of DEC’s global Working Groups.

Working Groups provide a setting for researchers and other stakeholders to examine important issues affecting higher education and digital education.

By contributing to these activities, fellows may gain exposure to collaborative research processes and international discussions surrounding emerging technologies and higher education.

This can be particularly valuable for postgraduate researchers who want experience beyond their individual academic research projects.

2. Contribute to Research Publications

Fellows will also contribute to the development of research publications on artificial intelligence and other burgeoning issues in higher education.

Artificial intelligence is developing rapidly, creating new research questions for universities, researchers, educators, students, and policymakers.

Potential areas of research interest may include questions surrounding the impact of AI on higher education, the adoption of emerging technologies, digital transformation, and the changing role of universities in an increasingly technology-driven environment.

Through participation in publication development, fellows can gain experience contributing to research intended for a broader international audience.

Why This Fellowship Matters

The higher education sector is undergoing significant technological change. Artificial intelligence has introduced new possibilities for teaching, learning, research, assessment, student support, and institutional decision-making.

At the same time, universities are facing important questions about how these technologies should be implemented responsibly and effectively.

The Digital Education Council’s fellowship responds to this changing environment by bringing postgraduate researchers into research activities focused on AI and other emerging issues.

For researchers interested in the future of education, this can provide an opportunity to connect their academic interests with current global discussions.

Potential Benefits of the Fellowship

Although the provided fellowship announcement does not specify a comprehensive list of financial or additional benefits, participation in the programme can offer researchers valuable professional and academic exposure through the activities described by DEC.

Potential areas of value include:

Research Experience

Fellows will have an opportunity to contribute to research activities connected to artificial intelligence and emerging higher education issues.

International Research Exposure

Because the programme supports DEC’s global research agenda and Working Groups, fellows can engage with research activities that have an international perspective.

Publication Experience

Contributing to research publications can help postgraduate researchers develop practical experience in producing research for audiences beyond their immediate academic institution.

Collaboration

The fellowship provides an opportunity to participate in collaborative research activities rather than focusing exclusively on individual academic work.

Understanding of Emerging Issues

Researchers can deepen their understanding of rapidly developing topics affecting higher education, particularly artificial intelligence and digital transformation.

Professional Development

Working on international research initiatives can strengthen a researcher’s experience and provide valuable exposure to contemporary issues in higher education research.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The fellowship is particularly relevant to postgraduate researchers whose academic or research interests connect with areas such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Higher education
  • Educational technology
  • Digital education
  • Digital transformation
  • Emerging technologies
  • Education policy
  • Technology and learning
  • Higher education innovation
  • Research into the future of universities

Researchers whose work intersects with AI and other emerging issues in higher education may find this opportunity especially relevant.

Key Areas of Interest

Applicants interested in the fellowship may want to consider how their research connects to the broader questions currently affecting higher education.

Some potentially relevant themes include:

  1. Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education
    Research examining how AI is being adopted and used by universities, educators, researchers, and students.
  2. The Future of Digital Education
    Research exploring how digital technologies are changing educational systems and learning environments.
  3. Emerging Technologies
    Studies examining technologies that could influence the future direction of higher education.
  4. Higher Education Transformation
    Research focused on how universities are adapting to technological, social, and institutional changes.
  5. Education Policy and Technology
    Research exploring the policy implications of new technologies in higher education.
  6. Responsible Technology Adoption
    Research examining how emerging technologies can be implemented effectively and responsibly within higher education.

Important Information About the 2026 Fellowship

Detail Information
Opportunity Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship
Year 2026
Organiser Digital Education Council
Focus Research, AI, digital education and emerging issues in higher education
Main activities Supporting global Working Groups and contributing to research publications
Target group Postgraduate researchers
Application deadline Monday, 14 September 2026

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026 is:

Monday, 14 September 2026

Prospective applicants should make sure they allow enough time to review the official application requirements, prepare their materials, and submit their application before the deadline.

Waiting until the final day can create unnecessary risks, particularly if additional information or supporting materials are required during the application process.

Apply HERE

How to Prepare for the Fellowship Application

Researchers considering this opportunity should take time to clearly connect their academic background and research interests with the fellowship’s focus.

A strong preparation strategy may include the following:

Step 1: Review Your Research Interests

Identify the main research questions, themes, or topics you are currently working on.

Consider whether your research connects with AI, higher education, digital education, emerging technologies, or another area relevant to DEC’s global research agenda.

Step 2: Understand the Fellowship’s Research Focus

Read the official fellowship information carefully and understand what DEC expects from researchers participating in the programme.

Pay particular attention to its emphasis on global Working Groups and research publications.

Step 3: Highlight Relevant Research Experience

When preparing your application, emphasize research experience that demonstrates your ability to contribute meaningfully to collaborative research activities.

This could include academic research, publications, research projects, conference participation, policy research, or other relevant work where applicable.

Step 4: Demonstrate Your Interest in Emerging Issues

The fellowship is closely connected to AI and other burgeoning issues in higher education.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate genuine interest in how emerging technologies are affecting the higher education sector.

Step 5: Prepare Before the Deadline

Do not wait until the deadline to begin preparing your application.

Aim to complete your application early enough to review it carefully and correct any missing or inaccurate information before submission.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026?

It is a new research fellowship programme from the Digital Education Council designed to support and expand its global research agenda by involving postgraduate researchers in its research activities.

What will fellows work on?

Selected researchers will support the design and delivery of DEC’s global Working Groups and contribute to research publications concerning AI and other emerging issues in higher education.

Is the fellowship focused on artificial intelligence?

Yes. Artificial intelligence is one of the central research areas identified in the fellowship description, alongside other rapidly developing issues affecting higher education.

Who is the fellowship intended for?

The programme is intended for postgraduate researchers. Applicants whose research interests relate to AI, higher education, digital education, emerging technologies, or related areas may find the opportunity particularly relevant.

When is the application deadline?

The application deadline is Monday, 14 September 2026.

Can researchers from outside one particular country apply?

The information provided for this announcement describes the programme as supporting DEC’s global research agenda, but it does not specify a particular nationality, country, race, or continent restriction in the information supplied here. Prospective applicants should therefore consult the official fellowship application information for the definitive eligibility and geographic requirements.

Conclusion

The Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026 offers postgraduate researchers an opportunity to become involved in an international research agenda focused on some of the most important issues facing higher education today. By supporting DEC’s global Working Groups and contributing to research publications on artificial intelligence and other emerging higher education issues, selected researchers can gain experience in collaborative and internationally oriented research. For postgraduate researchers interested in the intersection of AI, technology, digital education, research, and the future of higher education, the fellowship could be a valuable opportunity to expand their research experience and contribute to discussions shaping the next generation of education. Interested researchers should review the official application information carefully and ensure that their application is submitted by Monday, 14 September 2026.
